hero.sub: If your line clogs again a few months after every rodding, the pipe walls are still coated. Hydro jetting cleans them back to bare pipe with high-pressure water. We camera the line first and give you a flat price before we start. From our office on Esplanade Drive.

img.alt: J. Blanton Plumbing technician kneeling on a residential driveway, feeding a hydro jet hose into a sewer cleanout, with a branded service truck parked at the curb behind him

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Why Jetting Works for Algonquin Lines
blocks.intro: More than half of Algonquin's lines went in between 1990 and 2009, the age when buildup and roots catch up with them.

items.body: The trees planted with the subdivisions now send fine roots into joints. Jetting removes them more completely than a cable.
Algonquin's water comes from village wells. Groundwater minerals combine with soap and grease into a film on drain walls.
Kitchen lines in busy homes collect grease faster than any other drain.
We confirm the pipe can take the pressure and show you the clean result.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting worth it for a newer home?
items.preview: If clogs keep coming back, yes.
items.answer: If the line keeps clogging after rodding, yes. Even newer pipe collects grease, scale and fine roots that only jetting removes.

items.q: Can hydro jetting damage PVC pipe?
items.preview: Not when the pressure is set correctly.
items.answer: No. PVC handles jetting well when the pressure and nozzle are matched to it. We check the line on camera first.

items.q: How long does a jetting job take?
items.preview: A few hours for most homes.
items.answer: Most residential jobs take a few hours, including the camera passes.

items.q: How often should I jet my line?
items.preview: Only when the camera shows buildup returning.
items.answer: There's no fixed schedule. Lines with roots may need it every year or two. Lines that clogged from grease may stay clear for years with good habits.

items.q: What does hydro jetting cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on line length and buildup. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on how long the line is, how we access it and how much buildup there is. We quote a flat rate before we start.
